items.title: John Scott, Greenlanes addressed Council regarding the 2024 Budget.
notes: He indicated the proposed budget should align with the approved strategic plan priorities and would like more spending allocated to active transportation.
He further requested Council put a hold on paving projects unless they are connected to water and sewer projects to allow time to investigate more environmentally friendly options.

items.title: Land Needs Assessment Review
notes: Report from B. Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development
Presentation by Jamie Cook, Watson & Associates
Brett Salmon, Managing Director of Planning & Development indicated four scenarios based on density and intensification and introduced the consultant Jamie Cook from Watson and Associates.
Jamie Cook, Watson & Associates reviewed the four scenarios indicated the County’s Municipal Comprehensive Review (MCR) land needs assessment was considered the base scenario.
J. Cook responded to questions from Council regarding the risk of the loss of farmland and finding a balance between growth and the impact on farmland.

items.title: Environmental Registry of Ontario Postings Related to Source Water
notes: Protection
Report from K. Davis, Risk Management Official
Colin Baker, Managing Director of Infrastructure Services provided an overview of the report and reviewed the comments submitted by staff to the Province in October.
C. Baker responded to questions regarding proposed changes to stormwater and ground water protections.

items.title: Draft Plan of Subdivision and Zoning Amendment Decision Report -
notes: 6542 and 6560 Gerrie Road, Elora (James Keating Construction) and Township-initiated Official Plan Amendment
Report from M. Iglesias, Manager of Planning
M. Iglesias, Manager of Planning provided an overview of the report.
She indicated the site is 53 acres with a site plan that results 48 residents per hectare with a housing mix of single detached and multi- units with a total of 248 proposed units.
Staff responded to questions regarding traffic calming in the proposed subdivision and sustainability measures such as low impact development and construction.

motions.item_title: Draft Plan of Subdivision and Zoning Amendment Decision Report -
motions.text: THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington adopts a Township-initiated Official Plan Amendment to designate certain lands Core Greenlands and Residential to implement County Official Plan Amendment No. 69 to expand the Urban Growth Centre boundary and facilitate development of certain lands; THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington recommends to the County of Wellington that proposed draft plan of subdivision 23T- 18002, as modified, be granted draft approval, subject to the conditions of approval set out in Schedule "A" to staff report PLN2023-46; and THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington approves rezoning application RZ06/18 and that the appropriate zoning by-law amendment be given three readings.
motions.text_html: THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington adopts a Township-initiated Official Plan Amendment to designate certain lands Core Greenlands and Residential to implement County Official Plan Amendment No. 69 to expand the Urban Growth Centre boundary and facilitate development of certain lands; THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington recommends to the County of Wellington that proposed draft plan of subdivision 23T- 18002, as modified, be granted draft approval, subject to the conditions of approval set out in Schedule "A" to staff report PLN2023-46; and THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington approves rezoning application RZ06/18 and that the appropriate zoning by-law amendment be given three readings.

motions.text: That the matter regarding cannabis retail be referred to the Economic Prosperity & Growth Advisory Committee for review and report back to Council.

motions.text: THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington approves a single source contract award for the engineering design, installation and commissioning of an odour control system for the Clyde Street Wastewater Pumping Station to Environmental & Power Solutions Inc. at an upset limit of $383,007 including non-rebate HST, as outlined in Report No. IS2023-30. AND THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington approves an additional $1,500.00 including non-rebate HST from the Wastewater Capital Reserve to fund the anticipated project overage.
